Pre-Election Day Voting Options

  • Over the Counter Voting Schedule
  • County Office Service Schedule
  • Ballot Return Schedule
  • Voting Events Calendar

Voters may only return their own ballot unless they have completed an authorization form to return a ballot on behalf of someone who physically is unable to do so. For individuals requiring assistance in voting or returning a ballot, contact the Elections Division at 412-350-4500.

Voting Options Definitions

Over-the-Counter Voting
Over-the-counter voting is mail-in voting minus the mail. A registered voter can visit the County Office Building, (or a satellite office, if available) and apply for, request, complete, and submit a mail-in ballot in the same visit. Over-the-counter voting is also referred to as "in-person absentee" voting and “on-demand mail ballot voting.” Over-the-counter voting is required by Act 77, which introduced mail-in balloting to Pennsylvania.

Satellite Election Office
A smaller, temporary election office located away from the main one where voters can register, apply for a ballot, vote and return ballots. A satellite office is a location detached from the primary election office that generally offers a narrower range of services than the main office.

Ballot Return Sites
Ballot return sites are staffed locations, some temporary and some in the elections office, where registered voters who have completed a mail-in or absentee ballot can return the ballot in person, directly to a county employee. The ballot is then held in a secure location until Election Day, when it will be opened and counted.

Once the deadline to apply for a mail-in or absentee ballot has passed, voters cannot request a ballot on-site and may only return a completed ballot.

Satellite Election Offices

At satellite locations, voters may register to vote (through the state deadline of October 19, 2026) and apply for, receive, vote, and return their mail-in and absentee ballots. Any Allegheny County voter is eligible to vote at any satellite location. After the voter registration deadline (October 19, 2026) and the mail-in ballot application deadline (October 27, 2026) have passed, voters may still return a completed ballot at the ballot return locations. 

Voters wishing to apply for emergency voting must come to the County Office Building to make a request after those dates.

Election Services at the County Office Building

The County Office Building offers the greatest number of in-person opportunities to register, vote, and return ballots. Voters returning ballots in the last week before the election, beginning October 26, 2026, will be allowed to park briefly in the curb lane on Ross Street.

Ballot Return Sites

Ballot return sites are county-staffed locations where registered voters may return mail-in or absentee ballots in person. Using a ballot return site to deliver your voted ballot in person assures that your ballot is received timely.

The last day to apply for a mail-in ballot is October 27, 2026, at 5:00 pm. Voters may track mail-in ballots that are returned before Election Day to ballot return and satellite locations.
